newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul presidential panel proposes financial reform.
newsitem.headline: Seoul presidential panel proposes financial reform.

text.p: South Korea's Presidential Commission for Financial Reform on Monday put forward its final draft for short-term changes to the banking and financial system, a commission statement said on Monday.
The Finance and Economy Ministry now will review the 18-point plan, which was unchanged from the draft unofficially released last week.

The commission, composed of bankers, business leaders and scholars, proposed deregulation measures that would allow more opportunities for securities houses, merchant banking corporations and insurers to expand into banking.
It would allow over-the-counter derivative trades by all securities-linked financial institutions, and permit stock brokerages to engage in foreign exchange and commercial paper-related businesses.
Allowing merchant banking corporations and investment trust companies to become banks or securities houses was among the proposals.
The most controversial proposal is to allow the top five conglomerates to be represented on bank boards with non-permanent members.
The Korea Economic Daily said the finance ministry would oppose such representation, because of concerns about the conglomerates becoming too powerful.
But a ministry official said: "We have no official stance on this so far."
Other proposals call for establishing unified regulations on credit cards, instalment payments and the industrial leasing and venture capital business.

The commission recommended reducing bad debts of financial institutions by strengthening disclosure rules and allowing easier access to overseas financing by domestic companies and financial institutions.
The presidential panel will discuss mid- and long-term reform plans later in the year.
It plans to consider making the central bank more autonomous, liberalising new entry into the financial industry and permitting mergers and acquisitions of financial institutions.
